title: The past and the denial but...-š

blocks.text: With EGY present-03 tell your habits; with the past tell what happened: the weekend, the trip, yesterday's day. The Egyptian past is the perfect of fuṣḥā Without cases and with a little different vowels: katab, katabt, katabit. Denial surrounds the verb: ma-katabtiš I didn't write it. Study also the most frequent irregular verbs (ruḥt, šuft, ʾult, gēt), the expressions of past and smooth time just / not yet. Six weeks, in parallel with B1-09, B1-10 and B1-11.

rows: 8–9 hours · six weeks (weeks 113–118), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a tutor or Egyptian conversation partner, tutor recordings on the phone
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. to combine regular verbs and the most common irregular verbs in the past;
2. To deny the past with but...-š, even with the pronouns attacked;
3. place a fact in time (imbāriḥ, il-usbūʿ ili fātmin yomēn);
4. use lysa and lysa but...-š Not yet ʿumri ma- ... never;
5. tell what you did and ask others what they did.
Six-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).
Tuesday, tandem at the Polytechnic bar.

chapters.title: 2. The Egyptian past and the fuṣḥā

rows: no final vowel: you and I are the same
many verbs have instead of a in the first syllable

blocks.text: ana and inta have the same shape (katabt). The context or pronoun decide: an katabt / inta katabt.

The vowel that falls. In verbs in (i)širib, fihim), in front of -it and -u the second i falls: širbit, širbu, fihmu. Four-letter verbs (from derived forms): ištaġalt, ištaġal, ištaġalit, ištaġalu; zākirt, zākir, zakrit, zakru; Itkallimt, itkallim, itkallimit, itkallimu.
ištara Buying ištarēt ištarēti ištara ištarit ištarēna ištaru

The guys. 1. Concave verbs (rāḥ, šāf, ʾāl, nām): long vowel with people without consonant suffix (rāḥ, rāḥit, rāḥu), short with the others (ruḥt, ruḥna). 2. Verbs ending in vowel (miši, ištara, ṣiḥi Wake up: in front of the consonant suffix appears ē or ī (ištarēt, ṣiḥīt). 3. kal and ḫad: the hamza of fuṣḥā ( ⁧أَكَلَ⁩ , ⁧أَخَذَ⁩ ) is gone.

blocks.text: The vowel before -š. The -š wants a long syllable in front: katabt → ma-katabtiš (add i), katabu → ma- katabūš (the u stretches), katabti → ma-katabtīš. miš with the past is used only for a strong contrast or in a rhetorical question: miš ʾultillak? Didn't I tell you?

blocks.text: The -it of the female. katabit, rāḥit, ʾālit: one brief clear, not the a fuṣḥā. The -š that stretches. ma-ruḥtiš, ma-šuftūš, ma-kaltīš: the accent falls on the long syllable before -š. Repeat after tutor: ma-ruḥtiš / ma-ruḥtīš (f.). Shadowing. The tutor reads the dialog 2 with the tone of a worried mother; You repeat the lines of Šarīf, then those of Umm Šarīf.

exercises.title: Exercise 7 · What have they done?
exercises.instruction: Read the delivery and prepare your answer.

blocks.text: Listen to Script B and write for each person three things he has done and one that he has not done.

items.model:
Yāsmīn: she woke up early, went to college, finished her classes at 2:00, was in a coffee shop
with friends · she did not study at all (she was tired). Mīna: worked until seven o'clock, played football with the
team, he came home at ten o'clock and went straight to sleep · did not have dinner. ʿAmm Fatḥi: goods have arrived
new from Egypt (fūl, dates, bread), opened early, settled everything · did not sit a minute.
